ADR 0001: OIDC and Keycloak reference deployment

Status: Accepted — account verification and deletion administration implemented Date: 2026-07-31

Context

Pakperk must retain guest reading while allowing users to own synchronized saves and participate in moderated public comments. The application must not collect or store passwords. Native clients also need a safe token lifecycle and account deletion must revoke and remove the upstream identity in the reference deployment.

Decision

Pakperk is an OpenID Connect native client and resource server. Mobile uses the Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) in the system browser. The API validates tokens using OIDC discovery and JWKS, including signature, allowed algorithm, issuer, audience, expiration/not-before, clock skew, and a required subject.

Keycloak is the local, staging, and default self-hosted production reference provider. API authorization remains provider-neutral: verified (issuer, subject) values are mapped transactionally to a local user, and destructive provider actions are behind an IdentityAdmin adapter. Keycloak is the reference implementation target for that adapter; a no-op adapter is limited to explicitly incomplete tests/local flows.

Only refresh tokens and minimum session metadata are persisted in platform secure storage. Access tokens remain in memory where practical. Pakperk does not copy email into its database by default.

Implementation status

The provider-neutral verifier, publishable auth-readiness runtime, local account mapping, native AppAuth client, platform secure token store, reference Keycloak realm, and optional GET/PATCH /v1/me surface are integrated under ACCOUNTS_ENABLED. Guest paper routes are independent of OIDC readiness. The Phase 3 verification report records successful repository, native, live PostgreSQL, and real Keycloak/Mailpit acceptance runs.

The provider-neutral identity-admin adapter now has a bounded Keycloak implementation loaded only by the dedicated deletion worker. Startup obtains a client-credentials token and proves its exact manage-users grant with non-destructive reserved-user reads; redirects, wrong status/shape, oversized responses, and missing privileges fail closed. Session revocation and identity deletion are idempotent steps in the leased deletion state machine. Credentials are owner-only files and provider coordinates are encrypted in the independently signed restore ledger. Production enablement still requires the exercised realm grant, secret rotation, alerts, independent backup topology, and restore replay.

Consequences

  • Users can browse and read without an account; saves, comments, reports, blocks, and account settings require an authenticated local user.
  • Mobile must implement secure storage, single-flight refresh, reauthentication, logout cleanup, and idempotency-aware retries.
  • Backend configuration must include issuer, audience, allowed algorithms, discovery/JWKS timeouts, and a functioning identity-admin configuration when account deletion is enabled in production.
  • Pakperk gains a local user record and public handle independent of provider display data, avoiding authorization based on client-supplied profile fields.

Security and operational implications

  • Native clients are public: no embedded client secret, and redirect/post-logout URIs must be exact.
  • Token contents, authorization headers, OIDC subject identifiers, and emails must be redacted from logs, telemetry, crash reports, and local general storage.
  • Verification fails closed when required validation metadata is unavailable; unsigned tokens and token-selected algorithms are never accepted.
  • Keycloak must enforce email verification for self-registration, brute-force protection, password recovery, short-lived access tokens, and protected refresh-token rotation/session policy.
  • Account deletion disables the local account immediately, revokes upstream sessions, and then performs idempotent asynchronous erasure. Production startup must reject an enabled deletion feature without a working admin adapter.

ADR 0001: OIDC 和 Keycloak 参考部署

状态: 已接受 —— 账户验证和删除管理已实现
日期: 2,026-07-31

背景

Pakperk 必须保留访客阅读功能，同时允许用户拥有同步保存并参与受管理的公开评论。应用程序不得收集或存储密码。原生客户端还需要安全的令牌生命周期，账户删除必须撤销并移除上游身份，在参考部署中实现。

决定

Pakperk 是一个 OpenID Connect 原生客户端和资源服务器。移动端使用系统浏览器中的授权码流程（PKCE S256）。API 使用 OIDC 发现和 JWKS 验证令牌，包括签名、允许的算法、颁发者、受众、过期/未过期前、时钟偏移和必需的主体。

Keycloak 是本地、测试和默认的自托管生产参考提供者。API 授权保持提供者中立：验证的 (颁发者, 主体) 值被事务性地映射到本地用户，破坏性提供者操作由 IdentityAdmin 适配器处理。Keycloak 是该适配器的参考实现目标；一个无操作适配器仅限于显式不完整的测试/本地流程。

只有刷新令牌和最小会话元数据被持久化在平台安全存储中。访问令牌在内存中保留（如果可行）。Pakperk 默认不将电子邮件复制到其数据库中。

实现状态

提供者中立的验证器、可发布的认证就绪运行时、本地账户映射、原生 AppAuth 客户端、平台安全令牌存储、参考 Keycloak 域和可选的 GET/PATCH /v1/me 接口已集成在 ACCOUNTS_ENABLED 下。访客纸张路由与 OIDC 就绪无关。第三阶段验证报告记录了成功的仓库、原生、实时 PostgreSQL 和真实 Keycloak/Mailpit 接受运行。

提供者中立的 identity-admin 适配器现在有一个有界的 Keycloak 实现，仅由专用的删除工作线程加载。启动时获取客户端凭证令牌，并通过非破坏性保留用户读取证明其确切的 manage-users 授权；重定向、错误状态/形状、过大响应和缺少权限会关闭失败。会话撤销和身份删除是租约删除状态机中的幂等步骤。凭证是仅所有者文件，提供者坐标在独立签名的恢复账本中加密。生产启用仍需要执行的域授权、密钥轮换、警报、独立备份拓扑和恢复重放。

后果

  • 用户可以在没有账户的情况下浏览和阅读；保存、评论、报告、阻止和账户设置需要经过认证的本地用户。
  • 移动端必须实现安全存储、单次刷新、重新认证、注销清理和幂等性感知的重试。
  • 后端配置必须包括颁发者、受众、允许的算法、发现/JWKS 超时和在生产中启用账户删除时的功能性 identity-admin 配置。
  • Pakperk 获得一个与提供者显示数据无关的本地用户记录和公开句柄，避免基于客户端提供的配置文件字段的授权。

安全和操作影响

  • 原生客户端是公开的：不包含嵌入式客户端密钥，重定向/注销后 URI 必须精确。
  • 令牌内容、授权头、OIDC 主体标识符和电子邮件必须从日志、遥测、崩溃报告和本地通用存储中删除。
  • 当必需的验证元数据不可用时，验证会关闭失败；未签名的令牌和令牌选择的算法永远不会被接受。
  • Keycloak 必须强制执行电子邮件验证、暴力保护、密码恢复、短生命周期访问令牌和受保护的刷新令牌轮换/会话策略。
  • 账户删除会立即禁用本地账户、撤销上游会话，然后执行幂等的异步删除。生产启动必须拒绝在没有工作 admin 适配器的情况下启用删除功能。
